title: Declarative UI and component thinking
runtime: React 19.3 learning project with a current Vite setup. Version-specific commands must be checked against the linked React, Vite, and npm pages before use.

objectives.text: Compare declarative UI with step-by-step DOM commands.
Arrange components into a parent-child hierarchy.

learningFlow: Trace or change a practical example
Apply it in a fresh project decision
Review after two and seven days

diagnostic.question: What problem does declarative ui and component thinking help you solve?
diagnostic.answer: Name the relevant layer, its input and output, and one problem it does not solve.

sections.title: Describe the result, not every DOM command
sections.body: Imperative code tells the browser each change: find this node, disable it, replace that text, then show an error. Declarative React code describes the UI for states such as editing, submitting, success, or error. When state changes, React calculates the needed DOM update. You still write event logic, but the rendered result follows data instead of a hand-maintained sequence of DOM operations.

sections.title: Components are UI building blocks
sections.body: A component is a JavaScript function that returns markup for one part of the interface. Good boundaries often follow a meaningful visual or data responsibility, such as SearchBar, ProductList, or ProductRow. Do not make every div a component. Split when a piece has a clear job, repeats, has its own logic, or makes a larger component easier to understand.

sections.title: A screen becomes a tree
sections.body: A parent renders child components, and the resulting UI forms a tree. Start from a mockup and name the meaningful regions, then show which regions contain others. Data usually moves from a parent to children through props; later lessons explain events and shared state. The hierarchy should reflect ownership, not only visual indentation.

sections.title: Model the states first
sections.body: Before coding an interaction, list the states the user can see: empty, typing, submitting, success, and failure, for example. Decide which data distinguishes those states. Render each state from data, then connect events that change the data. This reduces contradictory UI such as a success message beside an active error.

sections.title: Use evidence instead of setup guesses
sections.body: When setup fails, identify the layer before changing code. Read the terminal command and first error, confirm the current directory and versions, check the browser Network and Console, and trace the entry file to the root component. Make one small correction, rerun the same check, and record what proved the fix.

interviewQuestions.question: What responsibility does declarative ui and component thinking have in a React project?
interviewQuestions.answer: Compare declarative UI with step-by-step DOM commands. Identify useful component boundaries. Arrange components into a parent-child hierarchy. List visual states before adding interactions.
interviewQuestions.followUp: What important responsibility belongs to another layer?

interviewQuestions.question: How would you debug a failure related to declarative ui and component thinking?
interviewQuestions.answer: Reproduce the smallest failure, confirm the current directory and versions when relevant, read the first terminal or browser error, trace the entry and root, and test one hypothesis at a time.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which evidence would make you change layers?

interviewQuestions.question: Which tradeoff in declarative ui and component thinking should a team decide explicitly?
interviewQuestions.answer: The team should match tools and boundaries to product needs, record version and deployment assumptions, and avoid treating a starter template as a complete production architecture.
interviewQuestions.followUp: How could the answer change for an existing server-rendered site?

commonMistakes.symptom: Every setup problem is described as a React error.
commonMistakes.cause: Browser, Node, npm, Vite, project files, and React responsibilities were mixed together.
commonMistakes.fix: Identify the failing layer from the command, URL, stack, file, or tool panel before editing.

commonMistakes.symptom: Commands work in one terminal but fail in another folder.
commonMistakes.cause: The current directory or active Node installation differs.
commonMistakes.fix: Check the path, package.json, lockfile, node -v, and npm -v in the same terminal.

commonMistakes.symptom: The starter template is treated as a complete production plan.
commonMistakes.cause: Scaffolding and build features were confused with routing, data, server, security, and deployment architecture.
commonMistakes.fix: Write product requirements and assign each responsibility to React, a build tool, a framework, the platform, or backend code.

publicationChecklist.note: Concept-complete setup draft. Recheck version-specific commands, run broader browser behavior checks, obtain independent review, and complete a learner trial before publication.
